title: The pro-'etale internal Hom for a site-perfect first variable
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\nu_X:X_{\Proet}\to X_{\Et}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism].

Let $a\leq b$ and $c\leq d$ be integers, and let $K',M'\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, respectively. Here Tor amplitude on either coefficient site means that tensoring with every $A_X$-module sheaf in degree zero has cohomology only in the specified interval; the pro-etale convention is [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Thus $K',M'$ are in $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$, the full subcategory of bounded constructible complexes with finite Tor amplitude. Suppose $K'$ is site-perfect on $X_{\Et}$: an etale covering makes it isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective constant-coefficient module sheaves, each term a direct summand of a finite sum of the constant ring sheaf.

Then $R\mathcal Hom_A(\nu_X^*K',\nu_X^*M')$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is bounded constructible on $X_{\Proet}$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and has Tor amplitude in $[c-b,d-a]$.

proof.text: The structure morphism $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type. The spectrum of a field has just one point and is quasi-compact: an open cover has a member containing that point, and this member covers the spectrum. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to $a_X$ to obtain an integer $m\geq0$ bounding its fibres. Its unique fibre is $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k\cong X$: the projection to $X$ is the base change of $\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$, with inverse $(\operatorname{id}_X,a_X)$. The other projection is $a_X$ under this identification. Thus $\dim X\leq m$, including when $X$ is empty.

source.place: Proof, first phrase: justify the dimension hypothesis needed to apply thm-sf-hom-ctf; Stacks Tag 0A3V

proof.text: Put $H'=R\mathcal Hom_A(K',M')$ on the etale site. Apply [thm-sf-hom-ctf] with $K=K'$, $M=M'$ and the dimension bound from step 1. The inputs are bounded constructible of the specified finite Tor amplitudes, the coefficient ring is $A_{E,n}$, and $K'$ is site-perfect on this same etale site. Its sharper clause gives $H'\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$ with Tor amplitude in $[c-b,d-a]$. In particular $H'$ is bounded constructible.

source.place: Proof, first phrase: apply thm-sf-hom-ctf on the etale site

proof.text:
Apply [thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible] to $K'$ and $M'$. Its first input is in $D^b_{ctf}$ by assumption; its second input need only be bounded constructible, which $M'$ is. It identifies the canonical comparison arrow as an isomorphism
$$\alpha:
u_X^*H'\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(
u_X^*K',
u_X^*M').$$
This uses the ordinary finite coefficient $A$-module categories on the two sites and the stated comparison morphism, without changing coefficients or assuming a formula for stalks of internal Hom.

source.place: Proof, middle phrase: identify the pullback by thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible

proof.text: Apply clause (i) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] to $H'$ and the interval $[c-b,d-a]$. It is applicable because step 2 makes $H'$ bounded constructible of that Tor amplitude, and $\ell$ is invertible on the $k$-scheme $X$: its nonzero image in the field $k$ has an inverse, whose image in every structure ring is still an inverse. The lemma gives bounded constructibility of $\nu_X^*H'$ on $X_{\Proet}$ and Tor amplitude in exactly $[c-b,d-a]$. The isomorphism $\alpha$ from step 3 transfers both properties to the required internal Hom. Explicitly its cohomology functors identify the cohomology sheaves; for every degree-zero pro-etale $A$-module sheaf $N$, the functor $-\otimes_A^L N$ carries $\alpha$ to an isomorphism, so its cohomology vanishes outside this same interval. This proves the asserted interval against all pro-etale sheaves, not merely etale-origin ones.
